properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-09-23, three rulings to finish step 4:
(1) FORK POINT WITHOUT AN ANCHOR — measured first: only 37 of 454 accepted decisions carry AT_EPOCH and only 4 of 268 epochs a checksum. When a decision has no epoch, the fork point is found in git: the first commit whose committed design export contains the decision, with that export's content_hash, labelled EARLIEST EVIDENCE IN GIT and never presented as when it was decided. Nothing is written on the read. Same rule as dec:temporal-backfill-from-releases: evidence from the repo, not reconstruction.
(2) REOPEN IS ONE CALL — a tool that applies dec:reopen-supersedes correctly: a new PROPOSED decision that OBSOLETES the original, which stays accepted and untouched, carrying the fork point and any doubt evidence as its reason. Run only on the owner's word.
(3) PERSON-AS-TESTER is NOT step 4 — who observed a result and how is about how results come in, and gets its own design.
properties.name: Finishing step 4: a decision with no recorded epoch finds its fork point in git as earliest evidence; reopening is one call; the person-as-tester path is a separate step
properties.rationale: Each offered with alternatives and a recommendation; he took all three. Rejected for (1): refusing (useless for 92% of decisions) and writing the anchor on read (a read that writes). Rejected for (2): leaving it as hand steps, which is how a reopen ends up flipping the original back to proposed — the failure dec:reopen-supersedes exists to prevent.
